R9767.summary: Sánchez's own despatch of 16 August 1523, not calendared: the new Doge (Gritti) 'no es mal frances' but can do little harm; the capitulation expresses no cause for the Venetian money, which the ambassadors always said was paid for the perpetual peace, not for any right of the Empire or the House of Austria; the Infante not bound to the defensive league; navigation rights for Austria not obtained.
R9767.en:
Since Your Majesty will see all that is happening from the letter that the Protonotary Caracciolo and I are writing
together, I will say nothing in this one except that I received Your Majesty's letter of the 15th of last month; and as
for keeping this new Doge in hand, I will do what I can, although, to tell Your Majesty the truth, one can see in him
that he is no bad Frenchman; but I hope in God that he will be able to do little harm, although it is well all the same
to keep him in hand.

Your Majesty will see by the capitulation that no cause was expressed why those of this Republic give the money to Your
Majesty;

R9769.summary: Joint letter of Caracciolo and Sánchez, 16 August 1523: the peace and league with Venice, departures of the English and Austrian ambassadors, prisoners freed, the publication of the league, the Friuli restitution and the 38,000 ducats, Milan's bonds and the 500 men-at-arms, Mantua, Ferrara and Urbino and the captaincy; after the date, Sessa made a Venetian gentleman and a cipher paragraph on the instrument of mutual restitution (no obligation beyond 'procuraremos'), and Milan news.

R9770.summary: Duplicate of R9769 (joint letter of 16 August 1523), with a short cipher at the head of the last page and a clear note on the "mutua restitucion" instrument.
